newsitem.title: UK: SW Water says on track to cut leakage levels.
newsitem.headline: SW Water says on track to cut leakage levels.

text.p: British utility South West Water Plc, posting a surge in profits, said on Thursday it was on track to cut leakage from its pipelines by the end of the decade.
South West said it expected to reduce leakage to 15 percent by the end of 1999 from the current level of about 21 percent.
Britain's new Labour government plans to set mandatory targets for cutting water companies' leakage to tackle the worst drought in the country in 200 years.
South West Water said it had accelerated its 99 million pound ($162 million) water distribution improvement and leakage reduction programme to help conserve existing reserves.
The company said it saw no need for restrictions this summer unless rainfall was less than in 1976 and water output was higher than the record year of 1995.
South West's annual pre-tax profits surged 22 percent to 132.6 million pounds for the year ended on March 31, including bid response costs of 5.2 million pounds.
The company increased its full-year dividend by 20 percent to 36.7 pence per share. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
